correctness.rationale: Encode each multiplicity s by nested binary indicators (1_{s>=1},1_{s=2}), so min intersection parity equals binary inner product; for k valid vectors RR^T=I_k. The strict k<2n follows from U_i dot V_i = V_i dot V_i, contradicting both columns being orthonormal in a square inverse. For k=2n-1, nondegenerate row subspace complement has z dot z=1 and projection R^TR=I+zz^T; the same nested column condition forces z=(0^n,1^n), hence n odd. Thus even n max 2n-2. Explicit families of 6 (n=4) and 10 (n=6) independently verified pairwise. For n<=5 independently enumerate ALL maximal cliques in the complete compatibility graph on eligible odd-parity vectors; counts 1,2,14,266,21574 and maxima 1,2,3,6,7. n=6 exact from bound+witness. Disjoint-coordinate union gives 10q+b_r. Finite exhaustive enumeration is only for n<=5, not infinite.
residual_risks: No exact O_2(n) asserted beyond n=6; only lower/upper bounds and asymptotic liminf.

Banerjee and Dewan, An Eventown Result for Multisets, arxiv:2610.21636v1
value.rationale: This is the smallest nontrivial multiplicity extension of Oddtown and asks a natural parity-extremal question left by bounded-multiset Eventown. The even-n codimension-one obstruction is genuinely structural; explicit first counterexample n=4, sharp n=6, and amplification to super-unit density 5/3 give meaningful boundary and asymptotic information, not an arbitrary small table.
residual_risks: Exact maximum still open n>=7; the asymptotic bound is a lower bound only.

final_claim: For two-bounded multiset Oddtown families in {0,1,2}^n with sum min(x_i,y_i) odd on the diagonal and even for distinct pairs, O_2(n)<=2n-2 when n even and <=2n-1 when n odd, first six exact values (1,2,3,6,7,10), and block amplification gives O_2(6q+r)>=10q+b_r and liminf O_2(n)/n>=5/3.
limitations: At multiplicity cap 2 and minimum-intersection parity; no exact larger-n O_2 formula claimed.
Deterministic exhaustive clique checks cover only n<=5; n=6 uses proof plus witness.
